Consult Summary:
- Adult with acute asthma flare presenting with wheeze and shortness of breath for 2–3 days; fever to 37°C; cough without sputum; limited ability to speak in full sentences; exercise intolerance.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Wheezy with shortness of breath for ~2–3 days; cough; fever (37°C); able to do no exercise; intermittent speech difficulty.
- Associated symptoms: Hay fever; eczema (history); no chest pain; no hemoptysis; no nocturnal wakings reported.
- Onset/duration/progression: Acute flare starting 2–3 days ago; symptoms described as recent and increasing activity-limiting.
- Past medical history: Childhood asthma; hay fever; eczema. Prior asthma requiring inhalers; hospital visits in past (not ICU-level). Last years: asthma largely inactive (stopped medications ~3–4 years ago).
- Allergies: None reported.
- Medications: Past inhaler use during childhood; currently uses salbutamol (inhaler) as needed; exact dose/route/frequency not documented; no current controller medication documented.
- Social history: Non-smoker; consumes about one glass of wine every 2–3 days; lives with partner; works as engineer; has been working from home or on sick leave recently.
- Preventive care: Not discussed.

Examination:
- Vitals: Not provided.
- Exam findings: Not provided.

Impression:
- Acute asthma flare-up likely superimposed on chronic history; possible triggers include environmental pollen or viral infection.

Plan:
- Medications/therapy:
  - Increase salbutamol inhaler use (two to four puffs every four hours initially) with use of a spacer (not currently owned at home).
  - Peak flow meter to be prescribed; spacer to be provided; pharmacist to teach proper use.
  - Regular antihistamine to be started (exact agent and dosing not documented).
  - When peak flow meter is obtained, record values: first thing in the morning and in the evening for one week; review results by phone to determine if additional inhaled therapy is needed.
- Follow-up and safety:
  - If fever worsens or wheezing worsens, call back promptly.
  - Possible initiation of additional inhaled therapy after review (pending improvement).
  - Schedule follow-up review in about one week to reassess asthma control and treatment plan.
- Education/other:
  - Pharmacist demonstration on spacer use when equipment is picked up.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Vital signs (temperature captured as 37°C but no other vitals).
  - Comprehensive medication reconciliation (current inhaler regimen specifics, daily controller therapy status not documented).
  - Peak flow value prior to this visit (not available; plan to obtain).
  - Documentation of allergy status is present as “no known allergies.”
- Internal conflicts: None identified.
- Transcript quality: Generally clear; occasional repetition and minor asking for confirmations, but overall coherent. No major inaudible sections.
